sanskrit: anantaṃ bata me vittaṃ yasya me nāsti kiṃ cana mithilāyāṃ pradīptāyāṃ na me dahyati kiṃ cana
english: Boundless indeed is my wealth, I who possess nothing at all! Though Mithilā burn, nothing of mine is consumed in the fire.

sanskrit: atraivodāharantīmaṃ bodhyasya padasaṃcayam nirvedaṃ prati vinyastaṃ pratibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this very point they recite this collection of sayings of Bodhya, set forth concerning detachment. Heed it well, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: bodhyaṃ dāntam ṛṣiṃ rājā nahuṣaḥ paryapṛcchata nirvedāc chāntim āpannaṃ śāntaṃ prajñānatarpitam
english: King Nahuṣa questioned the seer Bodhya, the self-restrained, who through detachment had attained peace—serene and contented in wisdom.

sanskrit: upadeśaṃ mahāprājña śamasyopadiśasva me kāṃ buddhiṃ samanudhyāya śāntaś carasi nirvṛtaḥ
english: "O greatly wise one, teach me the instruction in tranquility. Reflecting upon what insight do you wander serene and at rest?"

sanskrit: bodhya uvāca upadeśena vartāmi nānuśāsmīha kaṃ cana lakṣaṇaṃ tasya vakṣye 'haṃ tat svayaṃ pravimṛśyatām
english: Bodhya said: I live by instruction, yet I instruct no one here. I will declare its mark; let it be pondered for oneself.

sanskrit: piṅgalā kuraraḥ sarpaḥ sāraṅgānveṣaṇaṃ vane iṣukāraḥ kumārī ca ṣaḍ ete guravo mama
english: Piṅgalā, the osprey, the serpent, the questing bee in the forest, the arrow-maker, and the maiden—these six are my teachers.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kena vṛttena vṛttajña vītaśokaś caren mahīm kiṃ ca kurvan naro loke prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: By what conduct, O knower of conduct, may one wander the earth free of sorrow? And by doing what does a man in the world attain the supreme goal?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prahrādasya ca saṃvādaṃ muner ājagarasya ca
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they recite this ancient tale, the dialogue of Prahrāda and the sage of the python's vow.

sanskrit: carantaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kaṃ cit kalyacittam anāmayam papraccha rājan prahrādo buddhimān prājñasaṃmataḥ
english: O king, a certain brāhmaṇa was wandering, sound of mind and free of ailment, when the intelligent Prahrāda, honored among the wise, questioned him.

sanskrit: svasthaḥ śakto mṛdur dānto nirvivitso 'nasūyakaḥ suvāg bahumato loke prājñaś carasi bālavat
english: "At ease, capable, gentle, self-restrained, without craving to know, free of malice, fair of speech, highly esteemed in the world and wise—yet you wander like a child.

sanskrit: naiva prārthayase lābhaṃ nālābheṣv anuśocasi nityatṛpta iva brahman na kiṃ cid avamanyase
english: You do not seek after gain, nor do you grieve at not gaining; as though ever content, O brāhmaṇa, you despise nothing at all.

sanskrit: srotasā hriyamāṇāsu prajāsv avimanā iva dharmakāmārthakāryeṣu kūṭastha iva lakṣyase
english: While creatures are swept along by the current, you seem untroubled; amid the affairs of dharma, desire, and gain you appear immovable as an anvil.

sanskrit: nānutiṣṭhasi dharmārthau na kāme cāpi vartase indriyārthān anādṛtya muktaś carasi sākṣivat
english: You pursue neither dharma nor wealth, nor do you occupy yourself with desire; disregarding the objects of the senses, you wander free, like a mere witness.

sanskrit: kā nu prajñā śrutaṃ vā kiṃ vṛttir vā kā nu te mune kṣipram ācakṣva me brahmañ śreyo yad iha manyase
english: What then is your wisdom, what your learning, what your way of life, O sage? Tell me quickly, O brāhmaṇa, what you here hold to be the highest good."

sanskrit: anuyuktaḥ sa medhāvī lokadharmavidhānavit uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā prahrādam anapārthayā
english: Thus questioned, that sagacious one, knower of the world's ways and ordinances, replied to Prahrāda in gentle speech that did not stray from its purpose.

sanskrit: paśyan prahrāda bhūtānām utpattim animittataḥ hrāsaṃ vṛddhiṃ vināśaṃ ca na prahṛṣye na ca vyathe
english: Seeing, O Prahrāda, the arising of beings without apparent cause, and their decline, growth, and destruction, I neither rejoice nor am I distressed.

sanskrit: svabhāvād eva saṃdṛśya vartamānāḥ pravṛttayaḥ svabhāvaniratāḥ sarvāḥ paritapye na kena cit
english: Seeing that all activities proceed by their own nature and are bound up wholly with their own nature, I am tormented by nothing.

sanskrit: paśyan prahrāda saṃyogān viprayogaparāyaṇān saṃcayāṃś ca vināśāntān na kva cid vidadhe manaḥ
english: Seeing, O Prahrāda, that unions end in separations and that accumulations end in ruin, I fix my mind upon nothing.

sanskrit: antavanti ca bhūtāni guṇayuktāni paśyataḥ utpattinidhanajñasya kiṃ kāryam avaśiṣyate
english: For one who sees that beings, endowed with their qualities, are perishable, and who knows their origin and their end—what task remains to be done?

sanskrit: jalajānām api hy antaṃ paryāyeṇopalakṣaye mahatām api kāyānāṃ sūkṣmāṇāṃ ca mahodadhau
english: For even of the creatures born of the water I perceive the end in due succession—of great bodies and of small alike within the great ocean.

sanskrit: jaṅgamasthāvarāṇāṃ ca bhūtānām asurādhipa pārthivānām api vyaktaṃ mṛtyuṃ paśyāmi sarvaśaḥ
english: And of beings moving and unmoving, O lord of the asuras, and of those of the earth as well, I plainly behold death on every side.

sanskrit: antarikṣacarāṇāṃ ca dānavottama pakṣiṇām uttiṣṭhati yathākālaṃ mṛtyur balavatām api
english: And of the birds that move through the sky, O foremost of the dānavas, death arises in its due time, even for the strong.

sanskrit: divi saṃcaramāṇāni hrasvāni ca mahānti ca jyotīṃṣi ca yathākālaṃ patamānāni lakṣaye
english: And the lights that move across the heavens, both small and great, I observe falling in their due time.

sanskrit: iti bhūtāni saṃpaśyann anuṣaktāni mṛtyunā sarvasāmānyato vidvān kṛtakṛtyaḥ sukhaṃ svape
english: Thus seeing all beings pursued by death, knowing it the common lot of all, I, my task fulfilled, sleep at ease.

sanskrit: sumahāntam api grāsaṃ grase labdhaṃ yadṛcchayā śaye punar abhuñjāno divasāni bahūny api
english: A very great mouthful, if it comes to me by chance, I swallow; and again, eating nothing, I lie down for many days together.

sanskrit: āsravaty api mām annaṃ punar bahuguṇaṃ bahu punar alpaguṇaṃ stokaṃ punar naivopapadyate
english: Food flows to me sometimes abundant and of many kinds, sometimes meager and of few, and sometimes it does not come at all.

sanskrit: kaṇān kadā cit khādāmi piṇyākam api ca grase bhakṣaye śālimāṃsāni bhakṣāṃś coccāvacān punaḥ
english: Sometimes I eat broken grains, and sometimes I swallow oil-cake; again I partake of fine rice and meat, and of foods of every degree.

sanskrit: śaye kadā cit paryaṅke bhūmāv api punaḥ śaye prāsāde 'pi ca me śayyā kadā cid upapadyate
english: Sometimes I lie on a couch, and again I lie on the bare ground; and sometimes a bed in a palace is mine.

sanskrit: dhārayāmi ca cīrāṇi śāṇīṃ kṣaumājināni ca mahārhāṇi ca vāsāṃsi dhārayāmy aham ekadā
english: I wear rags, hempen cloth, linen, and hides; and at another time I wear garments of great worth.

sanskrit: na saṃnipatitaṃ dharmyam upabhogaṃ yadṛcchayā pratyācakṣe na cāpy enam anurudhye sudurlabham
english: What lawful enjoyment falls to me by chance I do not refuse; yet neither do I cling to it, however hard it be to obtain.

sanskrit: acalam anidhanaṃ śivaṃ viśokaṃ; śucim atulaṃ viduṣāṃ mate niviṣṭam anabhimatam asevitaṃ ca mūḍhair; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Unshakable, deathless, blessed, free of grief, pure, unequalled, established in the esteem of the wise—not approved, not practiced by the foolish: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: acalitamatir acyutaḥ svadharmāt; parimitasaṃsaraṇaḥ parāvarajñaḥ vigatabhayakaṣāyalobhamoho; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Steadfast of mind, never fallen from my own dharma, restrained in my wanderings, knower of the high and the low, freed of fear, taint, greed, and delusion: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: aniyataphalabhakṣyabhojyapeyaṃ; vidhipariṇāmavibhaktadeśakālam hṛdayasukham asevitaṃ kadaryair; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: With fruit, food, fare, and drink unfixed, with place and time apportioned by the turning of fate, a delight to the heart, unpracticed by the miserly: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: idam idam iti tṛṣṇayābhibhūtaṃ; janam anavāptadhanaṃ viṣīdamānam nipuṇam anuniśāmya tattvabuddhyā; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Having keenly observed, with insight into truth, mankind overwhelmed by craving—"this, and this"—failing to win wealth and sinking in despair: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: bahuvidham anudṛśya cārthahetoḥ; kṛpaṇam ihāryam anāryam āśrayantam upaśamarucir ātmavān praśānto; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Having seen in many ways how, for the sake of gain, the noble man here resorts wretchedly to the ignoble—taking delight in calm, self-possessed and serene: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: sukham asukham anartham arthalābhaṃ; ratim aratiṃ maraṇaṃ ca jīvitaṃ ca vidhiniyatam avekṣya tattvato 'haṃ; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Pleasure and pain, loss and the winning of gain, delight and aversion, death and life—seeing all of these in truth ordained by fate: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: apagatabhayarāgamohadarpo; dhṛtimatibuddhisamanvitaḥ praśāntaḥ upagataphalabhogino niśāmya; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Freed of fear, passion, delusion, and pride, endowed with steadfastness, judgment, and intellect, serene—having marked those given over to the enjoyment of results: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: aniyataśayanāsanaḥ prakṛtyā; damaniyamavratasatyaśaucayuktaḥ apagataphalasaṃcayaḥ prahṛṣṭo; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: My couch and seat unfixed by nature, possessed of restraint, observance, vow, truth, and purity, freed of the hoarding of results, and glad: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: abhigatam asukhārtham īhanārthair; upagatabuddhir avekṣya cātmasaṃsthaḥ tṛṣitam aniyataṃ mano niyantuṃ; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Having come to understand, and seeing how striving for gain brings on misery, abiding in the self, to rein in the thirsting, unsteady mind: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: na hṛdayam anurudhyate mano vā; priyasukhadurlabhatām anityatāṃ ca tad ubhayam upalakṣayann ivāhaṃ; vratam idam ājagaraṃ śuciś carāmi
english: Neither heart nor mind clings, as I keep in view the rareness of what is dear and pleasant and its impermanence—observing both of these together: this python's vow I follow in purity.

sanskrit: bahu kathitam idaṃ hi buddhimadbhiḥ; kavibhir abhiprathayadbhir ātmakīrtim idam idam iti tatra tatra tat tat; svaparamatair gahanaṃ pratarkayadbhiḥ
english: Much indeed has this been told by intelligent seers, by poets seeking to spread their own renown—"this, and this," here and there, that and that—who reasoned out a thicket of their own and others' doctrines.

sanskrit: tad aham anuniśāmya viprayātaṃ; pṛthag abhipannam ihābudhair manuṣyaiḥ anavasitam anantadoṣapāraṃ; nṛṣu viharāmi vinītaroṣatṛṣṇaḥ
english: Having observed all this—divided, severally embraced here by men of no understanding, unsettled, its shore a boundlessness of faults—I move among men, my anger and craving subdued.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ajagaracaritaṃ vrataṃ mahātmā; ya iha naro 'nucared vinītarāgaḥ apagatabhayamanyulobhamohaḥ; sa khalu sukhī vihared imaṃ vihāram
english: Bhīṣma said: That great-souled man who here would follow the python's vow and course, with passion subdued, freed of fear, wrath, greed, and delusion—he indeed would pass through this sojourn in happiness.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bāndhavāḥ karma vittaṃ vā prajñā veha pitāmaha narasya kā pratiṣṭhā syād etat pṛṣṭo vadasva me
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Kinsmen, action, wealth, or wisdom—which here, O grandsire, is a man's true foundation? Being asked this, tell it to me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca prajñā pratiṣṭhā bhūtānāṃ prajñā lābhaḥ paro mataḥ prajñā naiḥśreyasī loke prajñā svargo mataḥ satām
english: Bhīṣma said: Wisdom is the foundation of beings; wisdom is held the highest gain. Wisdom leads to the supreme good in the world; wisdom is reckoned heaven by the good.

sanskrit: prajñayā prāpitārtho hi balir aiśvaryasaṃkṣaye prahrādo namucir maṅkis tasyāḥ kiṃ vidyate param
english: For by wisdom Bali attained his end even at the ruin of his sovereignty, as did Prahrāda, Namuci, and Maṅki. What is found that surpasses it?

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam indrakāśyapasaṃvādaṃ tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this too they recite this ancient tale, the dialogue of Indra and Kāśyapa. Learn it, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vaiśyaḥ kaś cid ṛṣiṃ tāta kāśyapaṃ saṃśitavratam rathena pātayām āsa śrīmān dṛptas tapasvinam
english: A certain vaiśya, my son, prosperous and arrogant, struck down with his chariot the seer Kāśyapa, an ascetic firm in his vows.

sanskrit: ārtaḥ sa patitaḥ kruddhas tyaktvātmānam athābravīt mariṣyāmy adhanasyeha jīvitārtho na vidyate
english: Struck down, suffering and enraged, ready to renounce his own life, he then said: "I shall die. For one without wealth here, there is no purpose in living."

sanskrit: tathā mumūrṣum āsīnam akūjantam acetasam indraḥ sṛgālarūpeṇa babhāṣe kruddhamānasam
english: As he sat thus wishing to die, uttering no sound and senseless, his mind full of wrath, Indra in the form of a jackal addressed him.

sanskrit: manuṣyayonim icchanti sarvabhūtāni sarvaśaḥ manuṣyatve ca vipratvaṃ sarva evābhinandati
english: "All beings everywhere long for birth in the human womb; and within humanity, all rejoice at the state of a brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: manuṣyo brāhmaṇaś cāsi śrotriyaś cāsi kāśyapa sudurlabham avāpyaitad adoṣān martum icchasi
english: You are a human, and a brāhmaṇa, and learned in the Veda, O Kāśyapa. Having won this most rare estate, free of blemish, you wish to die?

sanskrit: sarve lābhāḥ sābhimānā iti satyā bata śrutiḥ saṃtoṣaṇīyarūpo 'si lobhād yad abhimanyase
english: "All gains breed conceit"—true indeed is that saying! You are one whose lot ought to content you, yet out of greed you set such store by more.

sanskrit: aho siddhārthatā teṣāṃ yeṣāṃ santīha pāṇayaḥ pāṇimadbhyaḥ spṛhāsmākaṃ yathā tava dhanasya vai
english: Ah, how fulfilled are they who have hands in this world! We long for those who possess hands, just as you long for wealth.

sanskrit: na pāṇilābhād adhiko lābhaḥ kaś cana vidyate apāṇitvād vayaṃ brahman kaṇṭakān noddharāmahe
english: No gain whatever is greater than the gaining of hands. Lacking hands, O brāhmaṇa, we cannot even pull out the thorns from our flesh.

sanskrit: atha yeṣāṃ punaḥ pāṇī devadattau daśāṅgulī uddharanti kṛmīn aṅgād daśamānān kaṣanti ca
english: But those to whom the gods have given two hands with ten fingers pull worms from their bodies and scratch the spots that itch.

sanskrit: himavarṣātapānāṃ ca paritrāṇāni kurvate celam annaṃ sukhaṃ śayyāṃ nivātaṃ copabhuñjate
english: They contrive their protection against cold, rain, and heat, and enjoy clothing, food, comfort, a bed, and shelter from the wind.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhāya ca gāṃ loke bhuñjate vāhayanti ca upāyair bahubhiś caiva vaśyān ātmani kurvate
english: Mastering the ox in the world they live off it and make it draw their loads, and by many devices they bring others under their sway.

sanskrit: ye khalv ajihvāḥ kṛpaṇā alpaprāṇā apāṇayaḥ sahante tāni duḥkhāni diṣṭyā tvaṃ na tathā mune
english: Those wretched ones who are tongueless, weak of breath, and without hands endure such miseries; by good fortune, O sage, you are not so.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā tvaṃ na sṛgālo vai na kṛmir na ca mūṣakaḥ na sarpo na ca maṇḍūko na cānyaḥ pāpayonijaḥ
english: By good fortune you are no jackal, no worm, no mouse, no serpent, no frog, nor any other born of a wretched womb.

sanskrit: etāvatāpi lābhena toṣṭum arhasi kāśyapa kiṃ punar yo 'si sattvānāṃ sarveṣāṃ brāhmaṇottamaḥ
english: With even so much for your portion you ought to be content, O Kāśyapa—how much more, you who are, among all creatures, the foremost of brāhmaṇas!

sanskrit: ime māṃ kṛmayo 'danti teṣām uddharaṇāya me nāsti śaktir apāṇitvāt paśyāvasthām imāṃ mama
english: These worms here are devouring me, and to pull them off I have no power, for I lack hands. Behold this plight of mine!

sanskrit: akāryam iti caivemaṃ nātmānaṃ saṃtyajāmy aham netaḥ pāpīyasīṃ yoniṃ pateyam aparām iti
english: Yet, knowing it a thing not to be done, I do not cast off this self of mine, lest from here I fall into some other, still more wretched womb.

sanskrit: madhye vai pāpayonīnāṃ sārgālī yām ahaṃ gataḥ pāpīyasyo bahutarā ito 'nyāḥ pāpayonayaḥ
english: This jackal's birth I have come to lies in the midst of wretched births; far more numerous than this are other, still more wretched wombs.

sanskrit: jātyaivaike sukhatarāḥ santy anye bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ naikāntasukham eveha kva cit paśyāmi kasya cit
english: By birth alone some are happier, while others are sorely afflicted; nowhere here do I see unmixed happiness for anyone.

sanskrit: manuṣyā hy āḍhyatāṃ prāpya rājyam icchanty anantaram rājyād devatvam icchanti devatvād indratām api
english: For men, having gained wealth, next desire a kingdom; from a kingdom they desire godhood, and from godhood even the rank of Indra.

sanskrit: bhaves tvaṃ yady api tv āḍhyo na rājā na ca daivatam devatvaṃ prāpya cendratvaṃ naiva tuṣyes tathā sati
english: Though you were to become rich, you would be neither king nor god; and even gaining godhood and the rank of Indra, you would still not be content.

sanskrit: na tṛptiḥ priyalābhe 'sti tṛṣṇā nādbhiḥ praśāmyati saṃprajvalati sā bhūyaḥ samidbhir iva pāvakaḥ
english: There is no satiety in winning what one loves; thirst is not quenched by waters—it blazes up again the more, like fire fed with fuel.

sanskrit: asty eva tvayi śoko vai harṣaś cāsti tathā tvayi sukhaduḥkhe tathā cobhe tatra kā paridevanā
english: In you there is indeed grief, and joy as well is in you; both pleasure and pain are there—so why this lamenting?

sanskrit: paricchidyaiva kāmānāṃ sarveṣāṃ caiva karmaṇām mūlaṃ rundhīndriyagrāmaṃ śakuntān iva pañjare
english: Cutting off the very root of all desires and all deeds, restrain the host of the senses, as birds are confined within a cage.

sanskrit: na khalv apy arasajñasya kāmaḥ kva cana jāyate saṃsparśād darśanād vāpi śravaṇād vāpi jāyate
english: For in one who knows no relish, desire is nowhere born; it arises from touch, or from sight, or from hearing.

sanskrit: na tvaṃ smarasi vāruṇyā laṭvākānāṃ ca pakṣiṇām tābhyāṃ cābhyadhiko bhakṣyo na kaś cid vidyate kva cit
english: You do not recall the taste of spirituous liquor or of the laṭvā birds, and yet there is found nowhere any food more delectable than these.

sanskrit: yāni cānyāni dūreṣu bhakṣyabhojyāni kāśyapa yeṣām abhuktapūrvaṃ te teṣām asmṛtir eva ca
english: And as for those other foods and dishes in distant lands, O Kāśyapa, which you have never tasted before—of them there is for you not even a memory.

sanskrit: aprāśanam asaṃsparśam asaṃdarśanam eva ca puruṣasyaiṣa niyamo manye śreyo na saṃśayaḥ
english: Not tasting, not touching, and not even looking upon—this self-restraint, I think, is a man's higher good; of that there is no doubt.

sanskrit: pāṇimanto dhanair yuktā balavanto na saṃśayaḥ manuṣyā mānuṣair eva dāsatvam upapāditāḥ
english: Men possessed of hands, endowed with wealth and strong—of this there is no doubt—are yet by their fellow men reduced to slavery.

sanskrit: vadhabandhaparikleśaiḥ kliśyante ca punaḥ punaḥ te khalv api ramante ca modante ca hasanti ca
english: They are afflicted again and again with the torments of slaughter, bondage, and distress; and yet even they take pleasure, and rejoice, and laugh.

sanskrit: apare bāhubalinaḥ kṛtavidyā manasvinaḥ jugupsitāṃ sukṛpaṇāṃ pāpāṃ vṛttim upāsate
english: Others, mighty of arm, accomplished in learning and high of spirit, take up a despised, abject, and sinful manner of life.

sanskrit: utsahante ca te vṛttim anyām apy upasevitum svakarmaṇā tu niyataṃ bhavitavyaṃ tu tat tathā
english: And though they are able to follow some other way of life, what is ordained by their own past deeds must come to pass even so.

sanskrit: na pulkaso na caṇḍāla ātmānaṃ tyaktum icchati asaṃtuṣṭaḥ svayā yonyā māyāṃ paśyasva yādṛśīm
english: Neither the pulkasa nor the caṇḍāla wishes to cast off his own life, though discontented with his own birth—behold what manner of illusion this is!

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā kuṇīn pakṣahatān manuṣyān āmayāvinaḥ susaṃpūrṇaḥ svayā yonyā labdhalābho 'si kāśyapa
english: Seeing men maimed, palsied, and diseased, you are fully blessed in your own birth, and one who has won every gain, O Kāśyapa.
